maya: quick heads-up — ran a small smoke QA comparing fp16 vs int4 quant for tundra-compact-1.0 on our short-query suite (<8 tok). seeing a noticeable recall@10 drop and cluster purity shift.
maya: fp16 recall@10 = 0.92, int4 (default sym) recall@10 = 0.86. long queries (>=32) basically unchanged. KMeans purity down 0.88 -> 0.80.
maya: eval cmd I used:
```
python eval/recall.py --model tundra-compact-1.0 --quant int4 --queries short_queries.txt --k 10 --index ann_ivf32 --ann-probes 16
```

maya: sample output snippet:
```
[recall] k=10 baseline(fp16): 0.919
[recall] k=10 quant(int4): 0.862
[cluster] purity baseline: 0.881 quant: 0.798
```

sanjay: thanks. did the embedding dim or normalization change in the quant pipeline? sometimes we forget the postnorm step when exporting quantized weights.
maya: good call — no, export kept dim=768 and we run l2-normalize after convert. confirmed the same pre/post norm. no accidental dtype cast in evaluation.
eli: could be outlier channels dominating quant bins. did you try per-channel asymmetric or kl-based clipping? int4 symmetric is brutal for heavy-tailed features.
maya: not yet. i have one quick per-channel asymmetric run queued. curious if per-channel int4 + 1% clipping helps.
cassie: also try running a small re-centering: compute mean per-dim on a 50k sample, subtract before quantize -> sometimes fixes cluster drift.
embed-ci-bot: nightly-eval started: job/vector-quality-smoke/2490011111 queued on staging cluster.
maya: update: ran per-channel asymmetric + 0.5% clipping. recall@10 -> 0.895, purity -> 0.84. big improvement but still ~3% gap to fp16.
maya: command for that run:
```
python tools/quantize.py --model tundra-compact-1.0 --scheme per-channel-asym --clip-pct 0.5 --out tundra-compact-1.0-int4-pc
python eval/recall.py --model tundra-compact-1.0-int4-pc --queries short_queries.txt --k 10
```

sanjay: solid. can you push UMAP of short-query vs kb vectors for fp16 vs int4-pc so we can eyeball drifts? scatter helps explain cluster purity loss.
maya: will do. plotting now and will attach gist when ready. initial glance shows a faint attractor shift for one category.
eli: if UMAP shows mode collapse on a few dims, try per-channel scale + bias (symmetric centers) or mix-int (keep final 64 dims fp16) as a conservative fallback.
cassie: let's add this as a short checklist for shipping quant models: 1) per-channel quant, 2) clipping sweep, 3) recalib mean, 4) recall@k short/long smoke, 5) umap sanity. add to PR template.
maya: agreed. i'll create a tiny checklist PR and attach the numeric deltas + umap png and the exact eval commands. tagging @sanjay @eli for review.
embed-ci-bot: job/vector-quality-smoke/2490011111: finished with status SUCCESS. artifacts: /artifacts/2490011111/ (recall.csv, purity.csv, umap.png)
sanjay: thanks maya — great reproducible notes. next step: run on a few different datasets (news, qna) and check the index sensitivity (IVF nlist / probes).

maya: on it. i'll run cross-dataset smoke and post results in this thread by EOD. :thumbsup:
